name: Cain Alvey
why: SGA's own Spring 2013 election candidate booklet. The heading 'Cain Alvey' sits directly above the studio headshot, in the President section, and the biography beneath it opens by saying he currently serves as SGA Administrative Vice President, which is the office the archive records for him in 2012-13. One name, one face, one block. Native size 299x331; not upscaled.
caption_quote: Cain Alvey is a sophomore special education major from Lewisport, Kentucky. He currently serves as the SGA Administrative Vice President

name: Ricky Jordan
why: The Herald's 2005 SGA election special ran a grid of senate candidates, each a single mugshot with the candidate's name set in bold immediately beneath it and their own profile beside it. His is the fourth cell of the second column, labelled 'Ricky Jordan', and the profile beside it puts him in SGA and on the academic affairs committee, which is the office the archive records for him in 2005-06. Cropped to the labelled cell only. Not upscaled.

name: R. Skylar Jordan
why: The Herald's spring 2008 election page ran four candidate headshots down one column, each with the candidate's name set in large capitals in a rule immediately beneath the frame: REAGAN GILLEY, SKYLAR JORDAN, KAYLA SHELTON, KEVIN SMILEY, in that order top to bottom. This is the second frame and its label reads SKYLAR JORDAN. The profile beside it says he currently serves as SGA chief of staff, which is the office the archive records for R. Skylar Jordan. The archive already carries the same photograph for its separate 2007-08 'Skylar Jordan' record; this is the same man in the year the archive lists him as chief of staff. Extracted at the page's native embedded resolution, not upscaled.
caption_quote: SKYLAR JORDAN | Jordan, who currently serves as the SGA chief of staff, has experience on SGA

name: Bill Parsons
quality: low: a 96 dpi yearbook scan, and the subject is shouting with his face painted at a pep rally, so it is a face rather than a portrait. Worth replacing if a calmer frame ever turns up.
why: 1989 Talisman p. 332, 'Tops come out at night', the Midnight Mania spread. The caption sits in its own box immediately left of the upper photograph and names one person; the frame has one face in it, a partial arm at the right edge aside. The lower photograph on the same page carries its own separate caption about Kappa Sigma members, so the pairing is not ambiguous. The volume's back index has a single entry for the surname, 'Parsons, William 332', which is this page, so no other Parsons in the book competes for it and there is no second page to cross-check against; the identification rests on the caption alone plus the fact that the 1989 volume covers 1988-89, the year the archive records Bill Parsons as SAFE Coordinator. Leaf 169, printed page 332 by the volume's 2*leaf-6 rule. Cropped to the photograph, not upscaled.
caption_quote: Bowling Green junior Bill Parsons is pepped for the men's basketball tournament.

name: Brandon T. Rucker
quality: small, 96 dpi yearbook scan of a studio portrait cell
why: 1994 Talisman p. 37, the Poland Hall portrait grid in the People section: rows of five studio portraits with the five names listed in the right-hand column in left-to-right order. Row one reads Lisa Pile Sr., Olivia Reed So., Randy Richardson Jr., Brandon Rucker So., Chad Schneider Jr., and the row lines up: the first two frames are women and the last three men, matching the name order, so the fourth frame is Rucker. The back index has one Brandon Rucker in the volume, 'Rucker, Brandon, 37', and no other. The archive already carries this same crop for a separate 'Brandon Rucker' record at 1993-94; this entry gives the same face to the 1994-95 treasurer record, which is the same man a year on (Poland Hall sophomore in the 1994 book, junior treasurer in 1994-95). If a later pass decides those two records are two people, cut this one and keep the 1993-94 entry. Leaf 20, right page; the printed folio on the facing leaf reads 'People 39', so the volume's 2*leaf-6 rule has drifted to 2*leaf-4 by this point in the book. Not upscaled.
